children.text: A square has four equal sides. Since you cannot break or bend sticks, the only way to form a square is if all four given sticks are equal in length.
So we must simply check if all given integers are equal.

In finding simple LNDS, all elements have the same "weights". But here we are given weights.
If we decide to keep an index $$$i$$$, its value remains $$$a_i$$$. Hence, the kept indices must form a non-decreasing subsequence of $$$a$$$.
Our goal is to minimize the total cost. Equivalently, we can maximize the sum of $$$c_i$$$ over the kept indices, since
Thus, the problem reduces to finding a non-decreasing subsequence that maximizes the sum of corresponding $$$c_i$$$.
Let $$$dp[i]$$$ be the maximum sum of $$$c$$$ in a non-decreasing subsequence that ends at index $$$i$$$.
For each $$$i$$$, we can append $$$a_i$$$ to any valid subsequence that ends at some $$$j \lt i$$$ with $$$a_j \le a_i$$$:
$$$$$$ dp[i] = c_i + \max_{j \lt i,\, a_j \le a_i} dp[j] $$$$$$
If there is no such $$$j$$$, we simply take $$$dp[i] = c_i$$$.
After computing all $$$dp[i]$$$, the maximum achievable sum of kept elements is $$$\max_i dp[i]$$$.
